reviewerSelfCorrection.whyItSurvivedMyPass: This is the sharp part. My v10 review did run a scan over every string field, and I described it in that verdict as the corrective for having missed two findings on v9. But the pattern was built for the v9 defect class — pre-D-169 language such as 'not live', 'until G31', 'naming v1'. It contained no self-version pattern. So the exhaustive scan I introduced to stop missing things did not cover the very class I was charging by hand in the same review. I generalised the previous mistake and not the current one.
reviewerSelfCorrection.standingLesson: When a finding is charged by hand, the pattern that would have caught it mechanically has to be added to the scan before the review is finished — otherwise the next instance of that same class is found by hand or not at all. For this review I added a self-version-identity pattern over every string field; it is what confirmed all three version tokens in v11 are correct, and it would have caught the v10 authorityClaim in seconds.

observationsNotFindings: The predecessorV8 repair is better than the fix I asked for. I asked for either the concrete form corrected to v11 or the generic form adopted; it took the generic form, and additionally recast the sentence so the version number appears only as history — 'v9 remeasured this after D-169'. Five sibling roles already used that construction and never went stale across eleven versions, while the two roles that named a concrete version have now produced three charged findings in this corpus. The fold removed a recurring failure mode rather than patching an instance of it.

Seven pre-D-169 hits persist and I again did not charge them, for the third consecutive version. The g32NamingV1 and g32ThreeLimbV1 roles say their candidates are 'Not recordable until G31 is live', a conditional whose condition has since resolved, and two G12/G21 reasons say 'does not record D-167'. All are historical entries about superseded candidates or still-true denials, the accepted successors are pinned alongside with correct standings, and this text is unchanged across v9, v10 and v11 with both reviewers declining it each time. Charging it now would be goalpost-moving on text I have twice declined. Recorded so the coordinator can decide whether the family wants historical roles frozen at their original tense or refreshed each fold — that is a convention question, not a defect.

This chain has now folded four times on provenance prose while the measurement itself has not moved since v9: obligations, flags and summary are byte-identical from v10 to v11, and the substantive remeasurement — OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION at DR-G32 — has been correct since v9. Every finding across v9, v10 and v11 has been about a field describing the world or the document, never about the leftover accounting. That is worth the coordinator knowing: the accounting has been stable and independently re-verified four times.

Both reviewers have now caught defects the other missed in this chain — Codex found two on v9 that I missed, and I found the predecessorV8 instance on v10 while missing the authorityClaim instance Codex's finding also covers. The dual-lane requirement is doing visible work here rather than being a formality.
